items.title: Knicks Bulletin: ‘It’s going to be bittersweet’
items.author: Antonio Losada
items.content:
Revenge game for KAT today?

I don’t think so, but who knows.

Here’s the latest before visiting the Wolves in still-not-overly-cold Minnesota.

On Rick Brunson’s decision to bring Jose Alvarado into the game against Toronto:

“Just a great call. Rick Brunson made the call of throwing Jose in to see if he can give us a spark. So, just a heckuva call by Rick Brunson and just a fantastic job by Jose producing on both sides of the ball when his name was called.”

On Karl-Anthony Towns improving his passing decisions and avoiding risks:

“It’s a fine balance because he’s capable of making some beautiful passes in tight windows so you want to let him be him. But I thought earlier in the year — and we talked to him about it, and said it a couple times — he was trying to make the home-run pass a little too much.

“And he’s gotten to a point where he’s mixing it up now. We’re going to trust him because he’s obviously done it for many years now with good results. We’ll lean on him quite a bit in that regard but if we turn the ball over too much, we’ll let him know.”

On Towns’ basketball intelligence and ability to read the game:

“KAT’s got tremendous feel. He’s a smart, smart dude when it comes to a lot of things, but especially when it comes to the game of basketball.”

On Towns’ coachability and the impact of assistant coaches Brendan O’Connor and Darren Erman:

“It’s easy to see where he is, because everything we’ve asked him to do, he’s tried to do. So, you’re extremely coachable. You got a great feel. And you got two guys in (assistant coaches) Brendan O’Connor and Darren Erman that are teaching you the game defensively at a really high level, and you’re starting to see the results of it.”

On the Knicks’ execution and contributions throughout the roster against Toronto:

“Our execution was at an extremely high level. We had a lot of guys contribute in a lot of ways tonight.”

On the Knicks early-season woes:

“It’s still a work in progress.”

On why the NBA must continue penalizing dangerous closeouts and landing-space violations after Brunson’s injury scare:

“They got to keep track of it because it’s going to happen. Everybody wants to try to block [Brunson’s] shot and every other guy’s shot. Some guys go forward too much and, if they do, there’s got to be a heavy penalty. Because if there’s no heavy penalty, then guys won’t be conscious of it. They’ll just keep sliding underneath guys.”

On why his shooting technique sometimes exposes him to dangerous situations:

“I fade a little bit. Taller guys are usually guarding me, so I got to be able to fade a little bit. Sometimes they’re not jumping straight up. They’re jumping towards me. It happens.”

On prioritizing getting buckets over worrying about landing on a defender’s foot:

“I’m not worried about falling on his foot. I’m more worried about if he’s close enough to block it. If he is too close, I probably won’t shoot it. If he’s not, ball is going up.”

On the Knicks rediscovering their preferred style of play against Toronto:

“We just played to the best of our abilities. I know the early season hasn’t looked like it, but that’s how we’re most comfortable.”

On the disappointment of not winning a championship during his nine seasons in Minnesota:

“I wanted to win one there. I didn’t accomplish that. But it was great to have those moments, to bring Minnesota back to the playoffs and be able to do a lot of things.”

On returning to Minnesota as an NBA champion with the Knicks:

“It’s going to be bittersweet. I’m just happy that I have such amazing fans and had such an amazing time in Minnesota. I love it to death. I love that place so it’s going to be cool to go back.”

On becoming a minority owner of Napoli’s basketball team:

“Napoli is a great underdog story and reminds me of what we have built with the Knicks in many ways. It is a project built around hard work, big dreams and the incredible passion Napoli fans have for their team. I’ve been coming to Naples and the Amalfi Coast for years, and I know what a fan base like this can mean to a team. Seeing this club already making noise in the EuroCup tells you where it’s headed.

“Matt Rizzetta and the team at Underdog Global Partners have high ambitions with a real plan for where this club is going. The Napoli journey is still very much in the first quarter, so I am excited to be a part of building this into something truly special in the years ahead.”

On Instagram after being demoted from starting center to the second unit:

“Nobody gone save me, gotta save my damn self.”

items.title: Demi Vollering, Eddy Merckx, Paul Seixas among cycling stars set for audience with Pope Leo XIV
items.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
items.content:
A host of representatives from the cycling world, including Demi Vollering, Eddy Merckx, and Paul Seixas, will attend an audience with Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican next week.

UCI President David Lappartient described the November 23 event as "an opportunity to strengthen cycling's commitment, as a sport, to promoting peace and intercultural dialogue among peoples."

Past and present Grand Tour champions are among a group of over 100 "distinguished guests" attending, in addition to organisers of all men's and women's Grand Tours and other races, and representatives from various cycling federations.

Vollering, Merckx, and Seixas will be joined by a host of current and former road riders, including Bernard Hinault, Annemiek van Vleuten, Greg LeMond, Elisa Longo Borghini, Francesco Moser, Miguel Indurain, Jeannie Longo, Vincenzo Nibali, Chris Froome, and Mark Cavendish.

Multiple para-cycling world champion Ricardo Ten Argilés, multiple BMX world champion Mariana Pajón, and Ukrainian cyclist Anna Kolyzhuk, who suffered a serious spinal injury in a crash during a race this year, will also attend.

Ahead of the event, Lappartient "highlighted the longstanding historical roots between cycling and the Catholic Church, from races organised by parish communities and cycling teams inspired by Gospel values, to the various meetings with Popes throughout the 20th century and the recent passage of the Giro d’Italia through the Vatican during the 2025 Jubilee."

The event will see Pope Leo XIV take an audience with the riders before the UCI symbolically donates several bicycles to Caritas Rome, a charitable organisation founded by the Episcopal Conference of Italy.

The audience isn't the first time the Pope and the cycling world have come together. In 2025, the Pope blessed the peloton ahead of the final stage of the Giro d'Italia, which started in the Vatican. The stage was dedicated to Pope Francis, who died in April.

Several other Popes have addressed the Giro in the past, including Pope Paul VI in 1964 and Pope John Paul II in 2000. Pope John Paul II also offered his support to the Amore e Vita cycling team in the 1990s and 2000s.

items.title: ‘Should Manchester United fans be hoping for relegation?’ Will Unwin answered your questions
items.author: Will Unwin and Guardian moderators
items.content:
As Mauricio Pochettino prepares for his first game in charge at Anfield, the Guardian’s Will Unwin answered your questions on Manchester United’s new head coach, the boardroom, the academy and whether Frank Ilett will ever get a haircut.

Every few months there is the report of a new “wonderkid” being signed: a South American full-back, a Scandinavian midfielder, a flying winger etc. But then they never seem to make the squad, let alone the first team. The same for our academy, which wins trophies regularly. Are there real prospects who could supplement or even improve the team? Is it too difficult to introduce them into Premier League games? Are they just investments for future sell-on? And why did JJ Gabriel leave?

The simple answer for many, and we can take the Paraguayan left-back Diego León as our example here, is that they are plainly not good enough and signing them has been poor . Some will take time, Sekou Kone was brought in from Mali and is out on loan at Lausanne to gain experience. Developing footballers is not an exact science and bringing them in from all around the world is a complex process to begin with. It is reliant on human factors outside football, of whether they can quickly adapt to life in a new country before even thinking about what they do on the pitch.

items.title: Black Friday Garmin deals - Big discounts on computers, watches and hardware
items.author: thomas.wieckowski@futurenet.com (Tom Wieckowski)
items.content:
Garmin products are some of the most popular items on sale during the Black Friday sales event.

Garmin bike computers, smartwatches, lights, trainers and other hardware are often discounted, and the Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales are often a good time to bag yourself a new piece of tech.

Amazon, Garmin and Sigma Sports in the UK all have a host of discounted Garmin hardware already, with some very good prices for computers and watches.

Let's kick off with the Forerunner 265? Want a quality smartwatch without going crazy on the price? This is it.

Currently at its lowest-ever price, the 265 will cover all of your running needs. You can also use Spotify to take care of your music, as well as just using it as a cool everyday watch. View Deal

The popular Forerunner 970 smartwatch is 13% off in three different colours. This premium running- and triathlon-focused smartwatch is geared to help you run and also provides HRV status and sleep metrics.

This bundle deal from Garmin also comes with a Power Bank included to help with charging when needed.View Deal

The fēnix 8 is 25% off already; this is the cheapest it has ever been on Amazon. There are also five versions to choose from in the 47mm face size variant.

The Edge Explore 3 may have arrived, but the Explore 2 is still available and is a good option for riders prioritising navigation features without a lot of other bells and whistles.

The Edge 540 is 14% off right now, though it was available for $244 last November. This is a good unit for all-around riding; keep watching to see if the price drops a little more. View Deal

The Edge 840 is at its lowest price in 30 days on Amazon right now, though it has been on sale for less cash this year. Officially, this unit has been superceded by the 850, but it's still a very capable unit with a touchscreen. View Deal

The Edge 550 is on sale right now with a healthy 20% off. This is a mighty computer, but we felt the lack of a touchscreen limited it slightly. If you are happy with buttons, take a look.

The Edge 850 is also on sale, discounted by 17%. In essence, this is the 550 with a touchscreen. It's a slightly bigger unit with a touchscreen, a built-in speaker and all the usual Garmin training and fitness tools. View Deal

The Edge 1040 Solar doesn't show a discount on Amazon right now, but it's $50 cheaper from the Garmin Amazon store than it is on their website sale right now, so I'm including the deal for you. If you want some Solar charging tech in a big unit this is a good unit. View Deal

The Garmin Edge 1050 is a top-tier Garmin unit and is arguably still worth buying over the recently launched and more expensive Edge 1060.

$100 off, this unit is a monster, with a brilliant, clear display and fast touchscreen.

This unit pairs a rear light with a Bluetooth radar to help you monitor upcoming vehicles from up to 153 yards away. If you want a built-in camera too, scroll down. View Deal

The Varia RCT715 is on sale in the US at 25% off. This unit brings together a camera, taillight and radar to help keep you safer on the bike. It Bluetooth-pairs with your head unit so you can view radar alerts.

The Garmin Varia Vue is 27% off if you want to invest in front and rear Varia units. This camera/light pairs a 600-lumen front light with a 4K camera to capture your rides. Tip: You will need a Micro SD card for the unit too. View Deal

The Flux 2 is discounted on the Garmin website; it's a solid smart trainer that prioritises low noise and is accurate within 2.5%. The trainer can connect with all the usual indoor training apps, so you can have a solid winter of riding. View Deal

The Tacx Neo 2T with Zwift Cog and Click is 18% off right now. This top-level trainer comes with Zwift's Cog and Click sprocket pre-installed, plus clip-on virtual shifters, so you can use it easily with any bike. It also works without power in standalone mode, which is useful for races, events, or outdoor riding.View Deal

Want to go the whole hog with a premium smart bike? Th Neo Bike Plus has a 10% discount. This is a fully adjustable smart bike that aims to offer the ultimate immersion indoors. The trainer vibrates and simulates road surfaces; dynamic inertia tech makes it feel like an outdoor ride, and the built-in fans mimic wind and keep you cool. View Deal

Garmin's latest RS210 power meter pedals are on sale. This deal is for the RS210 dual-sided SPD SL option which gained recharging capability over the previous units battery powered tech. SPD and SPD-SL pedal bodies can be switched onto the axles, and the pedals are accurate to within +/-1%. View Deal

The Forerunner 55 is a nice entry point into the world of smartwatches and has a healthy discount in the black colour.

This watch will suit runners, but will suit anyone just wanting a Garmin smartwatch with its two-week battery life. View Deal

This early BF deal sees the fēnix 8 drop to its lowest ever price on Amazon in the 47 mm/slate grey version.

The fēnix 8 is a top-level smartwatch with voice control and contactless payment tech. Its AMOLED screen is punchy and vivid, yet you still get up to 29 days of battery life in smartwatch mode. View Deal

The Garmin Varia RCT715 is at 15% on Amazon, the same as Sigma and the Garmin sale.

The RCT715 is a light, camera and rear radar in one and has daylight visibility up to a mile.

The Edge Explore 2 is a more basic unit that prioritises mapping and navigation. It doesn't have as many bells and whistles, but if that's all you need, it's a solid buy.

This is a really good price for the Garmin Edge 540. A solid little computer that's packed with a load of features. It doesn't have a touchscreen, so consider this point if it's a deal-breaker for you.

items.title: ‘Who is influencing whom and why?’ – Some of cycling’s biggest backers are spinning a sponsorship spiderweb, but what are the risks?
items.author: Chris Marshall-Bell
items.content:
At Spain’s biggest cycling races next year, one sponsor will be ubiquitous: Lidl.

Plastered across the red leader’s jersey at the men’s and women’s Vuelta a España will be the logo of the German supermarket chain; it’ll also adorn barriers and finish gantries at the Volta a Catalunya and the Itzulia Basque Country; and in each and every race, riders from Lidl-Trek, also emblazoned with the discount chain’s red-yellow-blue coat of arms, will be competing. Given the team’s big-spending habits of recent times, it’s not unfeasible that a Lidl rider will win (many) a Lidl race.

The newly announced sponsorship deals – which are in addition to the Lidl Deutschland Tour, and come three years after Lidl was a major sponsor of the 2023 UCI Road World Championships – are another sign of Lidl’s commitment and interest in mass-participation sport; alongside cycling, it has also significantly invested in football and handball. As the company's customer base and profits reach new heights, so too does its marketing strategy. To promote an active lifestyle to its millions of loyal and new customers, it wants to be seen as the supermarket of choice for athletes and active people.

But does Lidl further extending its tentacles into cycling pose a problem? Is there a risk that too much of the same thing risks threatening the sport? To get to the point: is there a possible conflict of interest issue to address?

Lidl is not the only cycling sponsor with fingers in many pies. MyWhoosh, the virtual cycling platform, has been a long-time sponsor of the world’s best team, UAE Team Emirates-XRG, while simultaneously hosting the UCI Esports World Championships. Similarly, MyWhoosh’s rival, Zwift, is the main sponsor of the Tour de France Femmes, while simultaneously sponsoring the Canyon-Sram team.

Elsewhere, French petrochemical giant TotalEnergies had a team competing in the Tour de France this year, while also being a major partner of the race itself. There are other examples: car brand Škoda, as well as bike component manufacturer Shimano, are also linked with numerous different cycling stakeholders. The list runs and runs.

It’s not a situation unique to cycling: similar multi-partnership arrangements are found in other sports, especially football. The UAE-based airline Emirates, for example, sponsors many of Europe’s biggest clubs, as well as the English FA Cup, the world’s oldest competition. Formula One can point to its own examples.

No evidence – let alone suggestion – has ever been raised of private companies interfering with the integrity of cycling competition. But has cycling reached a point where a select number of brands are spreading their wings uncomfortably wide, leaving open the possibility of them potentially having too much influence over the sport?

Power, success, and a particular image

Sponsors have held sway over cycling teams since bike racing began. Bike teams, after all, are funded by external backers, and they wouldn't exist without their support. Companies telling a team it must select X rider for X race for visibility purposes, as much as for competitive reasons, happened at the outset of bike racing in the 19th century and still happens today.

He and his team would say different, of course, but do you really think Tadej Pogačar has ridden the UAE Tour four times (and is expected to make his fifth appearance in 2027) because he views it as better preparation for his main season goals than, say, the more competitive and less sprint-focused Paris-Nice or Tirreno-Adriatico? It’s unlikely, but his appearance also serves the commercial and promotional interests of the team’s principal backers to have its headline rider in its state-supported home race. The story repeats across the cycling landscape: riders and teams make certain decisions based on the wishes, and sometimes demands, of those who provide the funds. There is nothing inherently wrong with that.

In the first quarter of this century, major international sponsors have shifted their marketing approach, favouring cross-promotion with similar but different partners to reach as wide and as diverse an audience as possible. "Companies realised a long time ago that sponsoring an event is not enough, as some have visibility but others don’t," Professor Jean-Loup Chappelet, one of the world’s leading sports governance academics, told .

"Sponsoring an athlete is better. It goes back a long way; look at Adidas and Nike sponsoring runners. They may sponsor an event as well, and there will be signs around the stadium, like there are on the road in cycling races, but the athlete gives them more visibility. As a result, every sponsor now does both: they have a team of athletes and sponsor events."

Professor Simon Chadwick, who is a leading voice on sport’s geopolitics and economics, concurred. "It’s about power and also projecting a particular image: we are successful, and we associate with successful sports teams and events," he said. "Emirates has the money and power associated with many leading football teams [and the UAE men's cycling team – ed], and they’ve successfully established a narrative that it and its associated clubs are the best of everything."

In a statement to , Lidl said of its various, concurrent relationships: "By partnering with various stakeholders… we aim to support the entire cycling ecosystem. This multi-layered commitment allows us to foster equal opportunities, prominently supporting both men’s and women’s cycling, and to bring the sport closer to a broader audience."

But do these spiderweb-like agreements constitute a headache for sports authorities? "Dense, highly interconnected and deeply embedded relationships exist that are increasingly throwing up contradictions and juxtapositions, meaning we get situations where people are asking questions," Chadwick continued.

"There is no doubt that there is evidence [in other sports] of commercial partners and sponsors seeking to, if not directly intervene to achieve outcomes that they are pursuing, then certainly trying to exert influence."

Evidence of sponsors directly impacting the result of cycling competition is in short supply. What appears more likely, and has been demonstrably proven in a wide range of sports, is that sponsors garner influence at a governmental level. That could mean they earn a seat at the table that decides venue selection for a tournament, or have a word in the ear of a committee member voting on regulation changes.

This is particularly relevant with Lidl: in the ongoing battle to reform professional cycling’s economic model and structural issues, understands that a Lidl employee is part of the UCI’s reform working group, while at the same time Lidl has become a shareholder in the team-led venture, Collective Cycling Group (CCG). That means the German company has a stake in both projects, which could give it influence over decisions that will shape the future of the sport projects.

"You can’t separate these things: governance, hierarchy, big networks, big money, the state, private equity investors," Chadwick added. "It’s become such a dense network that it’s difficult to even begin to unravel it or draw red lines."

The possible issues affecting cycling and the weight a small group of sponsors could have over the sport are worth spelling out – even if, it must be said, they are merely hypothetical for this essay, and there is no evidence that such incidents would eventuate.

If a rider is punished due to an in-race incident, could that team’s sponsor, who also has links to the UCI, use its leverage with the governing body to reduce said rider’s sanction? Could a situation also arise in which an event sponsor lobbies a race organiser to tailor a route towards a rider from a team that they also financially back?

Companies might not even need to wield such clout: those in charge of making decisions might be subconsciously swung towards a particular decision, aware of who is paying for the running of the event or the team. That is essentially how soft power works.

"Lidl operates with a strict, structural separation between its commercial marketing partnerships and sporting operations," a spokesperson for the supermarket said. "As a sponsor of race events, our role is strictly commercial – for example, focused on fan engagement and promoting fresh food.

"We have no involvement in, or influence over, race organisation, sporting regulations, or the decisions made by race juries and the UCI. The sporting integrity of the races is exclusively safeguarded by the independent race organisers and the sport’s governing body.

"When Lidl-Trek competes in a race where Lidl acts as a commercial partner, the team is subject to the exact same sporting rules and competitive conditions as every other team. The race organisers and UCI commissaires ensure an entirely neutral competitive environment. There is no structural or operational overlap between Lidl’s race partnership activation and the Lidl-Trek sporting department."

On the Collective Cycling Group, Lidl said discussions to strengthen cycling's long-term sustainability were ongoing and directed us to the UCI for queries relating to its reform working group.

When asked for a comment on the topic, Škoda said: "Škoda Auto has been a long-standing supporter of cycling and works with a range of partners across the sport. Our partnerships are based on clearly defined commercial and sponsorship agreements and do not extend to sorting decisions or competition outcomes. We respect the respective roles and independence of governing bodies, organisers and teams and conduct our partnerships accordingly."

Additionally, MyWhoosh's Director of E-Sports and Game Operations, Matt Smithson, said: "MyWhoosh is proud to invest across cycling, from our long-standing partnership with UAE Team Emirates-XRG to hosting the UCI Cycling Esports World Championships.

"Each of these is a commercial partnership with clearly defined roles. We have no involvement in team selection, results or sporting decisions in racing. These rest with the UCI, race organisers and the teams themselves. At the UCI Cycling Esports World Championships, the competition rules and results are governed by the UCI. We fully respect the UCI's governance framework and the independence of those who run and officiate the sport.

"Our aim is to grow cycling and make it more accessible to riders everywhere."

What's the UCI's stance on it all?

Speaking more broadly about the perceived conflict of interest, Chadwick added: "This gets to the battle for the soul of sport. What type of governance is there? Are there conflicts of interest? Who is influencing whom and why, and how are they doing that?

"Where is the money coming from, and why is it coming from there? What do people want in return, and who is taking what? That raises the fundamental issue of integrity: who makes decisions about rules? Sports fans need to know that rules are being created fairly and equitably, not on the basis of whoever paid to be a commercial partner. This is where we get issues around rules, bribery and corruption.

"In general, sport has made some progress in the past 20 years towards being better governed, more transparent, fairer and more equitable. But the reality is, despite all the deeds and good words, governance in sport is still really opaque."

In a statement to , the UCI said that it has a "clear governance framework to deal with potential conflicts of interest". It said that the "same brand cannot be the main sponsor of two professional teams at the same time", adding that "the principal partners and paying agent… may act in that capacity for one team only." Members of those teams, "which include its sponsors, may have no link with another UCI WorldTour, a UCI ProTeam [equivalent provisions apply to women’s teams] or the organiser of a UCI WorldTour event that is likely to influence the sporting course of events, or to be perceived as doing so."

There are examples in cycling of a sponsor’s logo being emblazoned on different kits: TotalEnergies on its eponymous team’s and Netcompany-Ineos’s; Red Bull, meanwhile, owns Red Bull-Bora-hansgrohe and is on the sleeve of Tudor Pro Cycling’s jersey. There is no suggestion that either sponsor has sought to favour one team or another in competition.

"When a company chooses to acquire sponsorship rights in several areas of cycling, whether teams, events or the UCI itself, this is a commercial decision based on the visibility each partnership brings to its brand. These rules are designed precisely to strike the right balance: allowing our sport to benefit from this investment while safeguarding the integrity of sporting results."

The responsibility to scrutinise potential problems lies with the UCI Ethics Commission, an independent body that reports its annual findings at each year’s UCI congress.

Biting the hand that feeds you

As the UCI alluded to, mid-sized sports like cycling that are dependent on sponsorship revenue just to survive, let alone thrive, cannot be too picky with where the capital that bankrolls athletes, teams, races and federations is coming from. "One of the core elements in this is the feeling that if we don’t agree terms with them [a partner] then they’ll go somewhere else," Chadwick said.

FOMO – fear of missing out – is real. "Of course it is," Chadwick adds. "But it’s not about a rival team or their riders, but a rival sport. You could sponsor cycling, but you could sponsor golf or tennis instead. Whoever secures that big money will secure a competitive advantage. It’s a common story across many sports."

The consequence of that is that it creates an uneasy situation in which the very questions being mused in this article are asked. "What always talks loudest in sport are not the governing bodies, athletes or fans – it’s the money," Chadwick said. "I remember once being with the sponsorship team of one European governing body, and I asked them on what basis they signed deals with partners. Was it an alignment with values, a particular target market, I asked. ‘No’, they said, ‘there's one criteria only – who pays the most’."

Ultimately, that gives further weight to the sponsors: they know that cycling teams and events are desperate for money, and thus often can’t risk an argument with their paymasters.

Yet perhaps this is all simply a case of making a mountain out of a molehill. Chappelet, who has spent decades researching sports governance, particularly in Olympic circles, suspects it might be. "I do not see a conflict of interest between sponsoring a cyclist and a UCI-sanctioned race organiser, or the UCI itself," he said.

History would agree with Chappelet. As previously noted, there is zero evidence of companies using their leverage to swing a decision towards their supported entity; it bears repeating, none of the hypothetical scenarios mentioned in this article (interfering in disciplinary decisions, venue announcements and course design) have ever been recorded, and nor is there any indication that such companies would look to flex their muscles in this regard.

And there’s another point worth addressing: if a sponsor like Lidl or MyWhoosh cut off its funding to cycling, would the teams or races it sponsors even survive? It’s not a guarantee that a replacement sponsor would step up. Don't bite the hand that feeds you, one might caution.

But as long as a select few sponsors continue writing cheques for riders, teams and the sport’s governing body, the uncomfortable, hard-to-breach matter of undue influence will persist in the background. Even with UCI frameworks that are designed to require transparent governance safeguards – and which, on the face of it, do just that – the reality is that part of cycling’s integrity is dependent on trusting in corporate financiers to act morally and ethically for the benefit of the sport and not for their own commercial interests.

items.title: NSN Cycling Team change bikes for the second time in three seasons as German brand returns to the WorldTour
items.author: Owen Rogers
items.content:
NSN Cycling Team will ride Cube bikes for the 2027 season and beyond after the team struck a deal with the German manufacturer.

Cube will provide the outfit’s World and Development teams with their Litening C:68X Aero and Air road bikes, while the Aerium C:68X will be deployed for time trials. The bikes will roll on Newmen’s Streem range of wheels, with SRAM providing the group sets and other components, while the saddles will be provided by Selle Italia.

Cube will be the team’s third bike partner in as many seasons. Factor provided their rides for a number of seasons when the squad were known as Israel-Premier Tech, but moved on at the end of the 2025 season, with Scott bikes taking their place for the 2026 season.

Now, with the arrival of high-profile GC riders, Primož Roglič and Richard Carapaz for the 2027 season, the team will be hoping for some stability, though it is a return to the familiar for their star sprinter, Biniam Girmay, who rode the brand’s bikes at Wanty-intermarché.

"We are incredibly excited to welcome Cube as our Official Bike Partner," said NSN’s General Manager, Kjell Carlström.

"From our first conversations, it was clear that we share the same vision and ambition. Cube's passion for innovation and commitment to performance make them an ideal partner for our team, as we continue to grow.

"In 2027, we will have more of a General Classification focus and the support from Cube will be fundamental to our success across the entire racing calendar.

"Of course, Biniam Girmay won three Tour de France stages and the green jersey with Cube, so we are looking forward to seeing Bini and his teammates create more memories."

Based in Bavaria, Cube were most recently in the WorldTour in 2025, providing bikes for Intermarché-Wanty, but when that team merged with Lotto for last season, they were forced out in favour of the Flemish squad’s Orbea bikes.

"From our first conversations through to the work already underway, we have been impressed by the team’s professionalism and its clear focus on performance," Cube’s founder and owner, Marcus Pürner, said.

"The team’s ambitions, reflected in its impressive new signings, such as Richard Carapaz and Kasper Asgreen and latest addition Primož Roglič, align closely with our own plans and long-term strategy.

"For us, this partnership also offers a valuable opportunity to work closely with the riders and technical staff, using their feedback and experience to support the continued development of our bikes."

items.title: Game Preview: Knicks at Timberwolves, November 19, 2026
items.author: Kento Kato
items.content:
It wasn’t long ago that a Knicks vs. Timberwolves matchup almost felt like a mini-rivalry—one of the few the Knicks had against a team from the Western Conference.

Given the East Coast vs. West Coast of it all, and the LeBron vs. New York effect, the Lakers made for a fun matchup. The Spurs and Knicks have had some tough battles, including the 1999 Finals and the 2024 Christmas Day game, and that pseudo-rivalry was elevated to a new level with the 2026 Finals. But whenever the Knicks and Timberwolves played each other over the last two seasons, it felt like there was more on the line than just the game. It was a battle for narrative, not just bragging rights. Which team won the Karl-Anthony Towns trade? How would former Knicks Julius Randle and Donte DiVincenzo play against their former team? Now, with the Knicks having won a championship and Randle moving from Minnesota to Brooklyn, this matchup no longer feels as personal.

That doesn’t mean that it’ll be a bad game. Nor does it mean that the Timberwolves won’t be a tough opponent. At 11-4, they enter Thursday night with a better record than the Knicks despite being without star guard Anthony Edwards since he underwent knee surgery on October 29. And contrary to expectations, their success hasn’t been a result of LaMelo Ball putting up insane offensive numbers. Their scoring has been incredibly balanced, with Ayo Dosunmu averaging 18.6 PPG, Ball averaging 17.7 PPG, and Jaden McDaniels averaging 17.1 PPG. Even without a single player averaging more than 20 PPG, they’ve managed to have the 12th-highest offensive rating.

Where they’ve remained elite Edwards, though, is on the defensive end. The Timberwolves, thanks in large part to four-time Defensive Player of the Year winner Rudy Gobert, have been incredibly dominant defensively. As of today, they have the best defensive rating in the league at 104, two full points better than the second-place Celtics. They rank third in the league in opponents’ field goal percentage, first in opponents’ three-point percentage, and force the sixth-most turnovers per game.

The Knicks, who haven’t completely gotten past their early-season shooting struggles, may have a tough time scoring against the Timberwolves. Even with the recent play of Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, Landry Shamet, and Miles McBride supplementing Karl-Anthony Towns’ dominant season, the Knicks still find themselves outside the top 10 in three-point percentage and near the bottom of the league in field goal percentage. That doesn’t mean the Knicks won’t be able to score, though. They have two very clear advantages heading into tonight.

One advantage is that they’ll have the two best players on the court. The Knicks can say this in a lot of games, and that hasn’t stopped them from getting off to a disappointing 8-6 start. And this matters less in the regular season than it does in the postseason. But this should still bode well for the Knicks. Brunson won Eastern Conference Player of the Week to kick off November and hasn’t really looked back. Even against a tough Raptors defense, he came through and put together back-to-back quality games. And you can make the argument that Towns hasn’t had a single game this season where he hasn’t been great in one way or another. The big man has also had some monstrous games against his former team, averaging 29.0 PPG, 14.3 RPG, and 3.7 APG while shooting 61.7% from the field and 56.3% from three. And in two of those three games, Towns scored 32 or more points and grabbed 13 or more rebounds.

The Knicks’ second advantage comes on the offensive boards. The Timberwolves give up the 12th-most offensive rebounds per game. Some of that is a direct result of their defense forcing so many misses. But with the Knicks being a top-five offensive rebounding team, Towns, as well as Andre Drummond and even Jordan Clarkson, could have big nights on the boards, making up for what could be an inefficient shooting night.

This will be a good test for a Knicks team that has earned seven of its eight wins against teams that are .500 or worse. The Timberwolves are 7-2 at home, deploy a dominant defense predicated on forcing players into the rim-protecting monster that is Gobert, and have a balanced offense that often scores just enough points. But expect the Knicks to lean on their two big horses. Brunson has also had some nice games against the Timberwolves and LaMelo Ball-led teams. And Towns has dominated just about everybody this season. We also can’t forget that the Knicks themselves have a good defense, which could test a limited Timberwolves offense. The Knicks come away with a low-scoring, ugly win led by Towns to improve to 9-6.

Who: New York Knicks (8-6) at Minnesota Timberwolves (11-4)Date: Thursday, November 19, 2026Place: Target Center, Minneapolis, MNFollow: @ptknicksblog and bsky

items.title: 'Passion has no age. Class is timeless' – Solution Tech-Nippo-Rali confirm Domenico Pozzovivo will continue racing at the age of 44
items.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
items.content:
Solution Tech-Nippo-Rali have confirmed that Domenico Pozzovivo will race on with the team next year, the Italian climber continuing in the peloton past his 44th birthday.

"Some riders are part of a team. Others are part of cycling history. Domenico Pozzovivo will continue racing in Solution Tech-Nippo-Rali colours in 2027! Passion has no age. Class is timeless," the team announced on Wednesday.

Pozzovivo, who turns 44 on November 30, has been racing since 2005, with next year marking his 22nd season as a pro. He retired at the end of 2024 as he and his wife Valentina welcomed their first child, Diana, before returning in April on a one-year deal.

Pozzovivo didn't race the Giro d'Italia in 2026 after his team didn't receive an invite, but he told that he's hoping to make a record-breaking 19th appearance at his home Grand Tour next May.

"Now I'm at 18, tied with Wladimiro Panizza, and... yes, I'd like to," he said. "Also because nowadays it's rare for a professional career to last beyond 12-14 years. So it would be a record that, while not unbeatable, could last a long time.

"Competition is the foundation of sport, and yes, I confess that it makes me happy. Finishing ahead of someone less than half my age doubles the satisfaction."

Solution Tech-Nippo-Rali look good for a Giro wildcard invitation next season alongside Polti-VisitiMalta, with Italy's other ProTeam, Bardiani CSF-7 Saber, not eligible for an invitation after missing the top 30 in the UCI rankings.

Pozzovivo would be a leader for the team if they are invited. He finished the season with the second-most UCI points of any rider on the roster, only behind Serbian sprinter Dušan Rajović, and this year achieved a series of eye-catching results at the age of 43.

Highlights of his 2026 season included third-place finishes at the Giro dell'Appennino, GP Beiras a Serra da Estrela, the Czech Tour, and a fourth place at the Mercan'Tour Classic Alpes-Maritimes.

"Between training and races, a million kilometres – actually, even more. At least 1.1 million. And I still haven’t stopped," he told .

"Training isn't a big deal for me, and I enjoy cycling. My performance, considering my age, is decent. So I turn the tables: why shouldn't I? Besides, I'm naturally drawn to challenging myself and my limits. That's the main thing."

Pozzovivo said that he had to negotiate with his wife to continue racing. He's balanced family life with time on the bike, while he has also completed his third degree (studies in nutrition sciences have followed previous degrees in business economics and sports science), with a fourth possibly upcoming.

"It was a fairly long 'negotiation', so to speak. When I stopped, at the end of 2024, one of the reasons was to be as close as possible to my daughter, who was about to be born," he said.

"But I started again because I realised that things could be reconciled, given that cycling is still important but no longer comes first. I'm trying to put it all together, and I think I can do it.

"If you love studying, and I do, it's right to continue doing so because staying up-to-date is essential – keeping up with the latest discoveries in practice. Specifically, I've delved deeper into nutrition sciences because it's something that, in endurance sports, now affects performance by 50%.

"Next year I'd like to take the state exam to become a nutritional biologist. To answer your question... Maybe, but I don't rule out the possibility that I might be interested in a Master's degree."

Now, however, Pozzovivo will turn his focus to training for 2027 and that possible return to the Giro d'Italia, where he's finished in the top 10 on seven occasions. Will it be his final season on the bike?

"We'll see. It's not a given," he concluded.

items.title: Tour de Romandie saved as Primeo Energie steps in as sponsor for both women’s and men’s races
items.author: Owen Rogers
items.content:
After a lack of funds was cited as a major contributing factor in the cancellation of the 2026 Tour de Romandie Féminin, the race will return in 2027 with Primeo Energie stepping up to sponsor both women’s and men’s races.

The Swiss electricity company have sponsored the races’ mountains classification jerseys since 2022, the first year of the women’s race, but will now be the main sponsor of both events for the next two editions.

Even before the 2026 race, the organisation was in trouble, hoping to address a 10% budget shortfall by attracting Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates). But a week after he won four of the five stages and the general classification, organisers, Chassot Concept SA, announced the postponement of the 2026 women’s race.

"This postponement also aims to preserve the Foundation's financial stability and, ultimately, to guarantee the quality and long-term viability of the event," organisers said at the time.

Now, with Primeo Energie on board, not only is the men’s race secure, but the women’s event will return in 2027, with the three-day stage race due to start on September 10th.

"We have seen just how deeply the Tour de Romandie is rooted in the hearts of the people of French-speaking Switzerland," Primeo Energie’s CEO, Cédric Christmann, said. "We are strengthening our presence in a region where we intend to continue our growth.

"Supporting the women’s race is also particularly important to me; women’s cycling deserves more attention - much like the energy sector, especially regarding technical roles and leadership positions."

Unlike the men’s race, which began in 1947, the women’s race has a short history, starting as recently as 2022. Then Ashleigh Moolman-Pasio beat Annemiek van Vleuten on the mountain stage to the ski centre at Thyon 2000, going on to take the only WorldTour general classification success of her career.

Held in 2025, the most recent edition was won by home rider Elise Chabby (FDJ-SUEZ). The race also witnessed the emergence of Paula Blasi, who won the opening day mountain time trial, collecting her first WorldTour victory. However, the race was undermined when five teams were excluded from the race before the start.

While details of the women’s race are yet to be released, organisers chose the sponsorship announcement to publish details of the 80th edition of the men’s race, which will start with its traditional prologue on Tuesday, April 27 and feature a number of circuit-based stages.

"We have opted for loop-style stages, with each one taking place almost entirely within a single canton," said organiser Richard Chassot.

"This allows the public to see the riders multiple times in a festive atmosphere. This format also addresses safety requirements, which are becoming increasingly complex and costly."

  • Prologue - Yverdon-les-Bains (4.7km)
  • Stage 1 - Romont - Romont (170.1km)
  • Stage 2 - La Chaux-de-Fonds - La Chauxde-Fonds (176.2km)
  • Stage 3 - Vully-les-Lacs - Vully-les-Lacs, ITT (14.6km)

items.title: Tour Colombia returns for 2027 after two-year break with multiple WorldTour teams expected to race
items.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
items.content:
The early-season Tour Colombia returns to the calendar in 2027, with the race's fifth edition set to run January 26-31.

The race was founded in 2018 as the Colombia Oro y Paz and has run editions in 2019, 2020, and 2024. It was cancelled in both 2025 and 2026 due to financial difficulties.

It's back next season, however, with its return announced in September. Last week, the race was unveiled in a presentation in Medellín attended by former winners Egan Bernal and Sergio Higuita, as well as a host of other Colombian cycling stars, including Santiago Buitrago, Fernando Gaviria, Nairo Quintana, and Rigoberto Urán.

This week, the route for the 2.1-ranked race was unveiled, and the first teams confirmed to take part were also announced.

Colombian outlet has revealed that WorldTour teams Netcompany Ineos and EF Education-EasyPost will be taking part. It's likely, then, that Bernal, Harold Tejada, Iván Sosa, and Juan Felipe Rodríguez will be racing.

US squad Modern Adventure Pro Cycling will also be on the start line, as will Colombian Continental squads NU Colombia (the team of 2024 champion Rodrigo Contreras), Medellín-EPM (featuring Óscar Sevilla), GW Sportfitness, Sistecrédito, and Orgullo Paisa.

reports that NSN, Movistar, and Caja Rural-Seguros RGA could also be at the start.

The most recent edition in 2024 saw Contreras take overall victory by six seconds from Richard Carapaz, then racing for EF, as Mark Cavendish, Nairo Quintana, and Alexey Lutsenko also took part.

Those who are racing will face a six-day run from Medellín to the final summit finish atop the Alto de Palmas. The 904.2km route will be confined to the Antioquia region, with the toughest stages coming in the last two days of the race, including a penultimate stage finish atop the climb to the Alto la Unión.

items.title: 'A bold new visual era' for the maglia rosa as MAAP strikes deal to produce Giro d'Italia leaders' jerseys
items.author: Owen Rogers
items.content:
Australian cycling kit company MAAP is promising an eye-catching revamp of the Giro d’Italia leaders’ jerseys after agreeing a multi-year partnership with organisers RCS to provide apparel across their range of races.

As well as the men’s and women's Giro d'Italia, the agreement will also see the brand providing jerseys for RCS’s other Italian stage races, including Tirreno Adriatico and the Giro Next Gen.

There will also be jerseys for one-day events like Milan-San Remo, Strade Bianche, and Il Lombardia, though they won’t be worn in the race or awarded to winners.

MAAP, which was only founded in 2014, first entered the European pro peloton in 2024, producing a striking design for women’s Continental team Lifeplus-Wahoo, before going further with the current purple Jayco-AlUla and Liv-AlUla Jayco team kits.

To continue in that eye-catching vein, MAAP is promising "a bold new visual era for the most beautiful Grand Tours".

understands the new pink jersey design for men’s and women’s Giro d'Italia will be a significant departure from the old produced by Castelli, though it will not be revealed until sometime in the New Year.

"The partnership seeks to bridge the deep traditions of European racing with contemporary culture through performance and design," MAAP’s press release states.

"Bringing a progressive perspective to some of cycling's most iconic symbols, MAAP will honour the heritage of these events while challenging conventions through a new approach to technical apparel and visual expression."

It’s been a remarkable rise for MAAP, which was founded in 2014 in the Australian city of Melbourne and has always produced kit that looks a little different to that of other companies. Their first team partnership was for Australian Continental team State of the Matter, before partnering with Trinity Racing in 2019.

"From the start, we set out to make the world’s best cycling apparel, paired with a design language that lights up the sport," said company founder Jarrad Smith.

"The Giro d’Italia has shaped the performance and aesthetic of cycling for more than a century, and it holds a special place in my heart. It’s the race that got me into road cycling. Stepping into that living history, and helping progress the Maglia Rosa and some of cycling’s most storied races, is a defining milestone and a privilege. It’s also a statement of our respect for the sport’s history and our passion for where it can go."

CEO and General Manager of RCS Sports and Events Paolo Bellino said: "MAAP is a young and ambitious company, it stands out for its use of technologically advanced materials and its strong design identity. We are confident that the new jerseys, which will be unveiled soon, will generate great interest among all cycling fans, and particularly among younger generations.

"We hope that this partnership with MAAP will lead us into a new era, one that is even more modern and innovative, while continuing to respect the great tradition of the Giro d’Italia and our races."

The deal comes hot on the heels of Castelli’s partnership and sponsorship agreement with ASO to provide leaders’ jerseys for the Tour de France, Tour de France Femmes and their other races, including both men’s and women’s Vuelta a España, though it is thought the sponsorship element of MAAP’s deal is absent.

items.title: The longest single-opponent winning streaks in Knicks history
items.author: Michael Zeno
items.content:
On Tuesday night, the Knicks outlasted the Raptors for the second time in three nights to extend a staggering 15-game winning streak against their Canadian rivals that dates back to January 2023.

Beyond the fact that it means that old friends RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley have never beaten their old team, it also extends one of the longest streaks in program history against a single opponent.

Celtics, 21 games (1993-98)

As mentioned on last night’s broadcast, it’s hard to believe such a dominant stretch existed against a longtime rival that has been the Eastern Conference’s banner of success for generations.

Simply, the sport is cyclical, and the few times the Celtics were in the doldrums, the Knicks were contending for titles. Through the many dark ages of Knicks history, the Celtics dominated. It’s why they’ve only faced off in the postseason three times in the last 35 years.

From 1965-67, the Celtics won 21 in a row against the Knicks in the heart of the Bill Russell era. It took 25 years to return the favor.

On January 10, 1993, the Celtics outlasted the Knicks at TD Garden in a 100-97 win. They wouldn’t win another game in this rivalry for over five years.

The Celtics won 48 games in 1992-93, but quickly fell into the East’s cellar. They wouldn’t win 40 games again in a season until 2001-02, while at the same time, Patrick Ewing and the Knicks had only the Bulls and Pacers competing with them for spots in the NBA Finals yearly.

Ewing would score 65 combined over the next two meetings in April 1993 before scoring 30 again on Opening Night that October in a three-point win in Boston. He routinely owned the Celtics during this time, reaching a crescendo with a 36-14 effort in March 1994.

As the Celtics got worse, the Knicks took advantage of them more and more. A 35-point blowout in February 1994 still stands as one of the biggest blowouts in the rivalry’s history. Hubert Davis nailed five threes and scored 25 points in a 90-83 win the following month.

It was always a different enemy that flummoxed the Celtics. Charles Smith scoring 25, Anthony Mason scoring 21, and John Starks and Ewing’s consistency. Even as Pat Riley turned into Jeff Van Gundy, the Knicks never lost a step.

The streak had reached 17 by January 28, 1997, when the pitiful 9-30 Celtics put the greatest scare into the contending Knicks yet. An eight-point lead in the final minutes dwindled to a tie on a Todd Day three in the final minute before free throws by Antoine Walker gave Boston the lead in the final minute.

Just when the streak appeared over, Chris Childs called game with eight seconds left.

Eventually, the streak would finally end on January 26, 1998, when the Knicks were held to just 85 points behind a 25-point gem by Chauncey Billups. Even this triumphant victory came with an asterisk, as Ewing missed the game due to wrist surgery. Huh.

Cavaliers, 18 games (1980-83)

The Knicks own the Cavs in the playoffs, but did you know there was a stretch they owned them like

In five all-time playoff meetings, the Knicks are 16-2 against the Cavs, but once took things to another level in the early 1980s.

Unlike the Celtics, this is pretty peculiar. The Knicks were an average team during this streak, but took advantage of one of the worst eras of Cavs basketball under Ted Stepien.

Quite precisely, this streak can be known as the “Stepien Streak”, as while he was owner from April 1980 to his sale in April 1983, the Cavs went 1-16 against the Knicks, with the lone win coming just two weeks before he sold the team in late March of 1983.

Highlights of the streak include Mike Glenn’s 29-point game in November 1980 (second-highest scoring game of his career), Ray Williams’ 37-point gem in an overtime win two weeks later, and perennially playing in front of 4,000 fans at an empty Richfield Coliseum. The NBA was totally different in the 80s.

Bullets, 17 games (1952-53)

Back in the day, there weren’t many teams. As such, you get stuff like this.

Over a span of 400 days from February 6, 1952, to March 11, 1953, the Knicks played the Baltimore Bullets 17 times and won every single one of them.

The 1950s Knicks can sometimes be referred to as the Silver Era of Knicks basketball due to the team making multiple Finals appearances before Russell came and made the East his own, so it’s no surprise they were dominant. But like this?

The lore of 1950s NBA is quite fascinating. These teams played each other three times in six days in February 1952 when the streak began, but played the games in three different places. The Bullets won 82-81 in the Baltimore Coliseum on February 4, the Knicks won 73-70 at the 69th Regiment Armory on February 6, and the two teams met in Philadelphia on February 8 in a 20-point blowout win for Ray Lumpp and the Knicks.

On March 5, the teams participated in a doubleheader at the Boston Garden, preceding a game between the Bucks and Celtics later that night.

In 1952-53, when the Knicks went 10-0 against the Bullets en route to a Finals appearance, they played one game in Philly, two games in Boston (one of which went to triple overtime), and even played in Trenton, New Jersey, on March 5, 1953.

Finally, the Bullets snapped the skid on November 14, 1953, behind 19 points by Max Zaslofsky in Baltimore.

Just for the hell of it, here’s some other weird neutral site locations from the 1950s:

  • January 29, 1952, in Louisville (vs. Indianapolis Olympians)
  • February 3, 1953, in Buffalo (vs. Milwaukee Hawks)
  • February 18, 1953, in Providence (vs. Boston Celtics)
  • January 22, 1954, in New Haven, CT (vs. Philadelphia Warriors)
  • Several times in 1954-55 in Miami (vs. Fort Wayne Pistons)
  • November 18, 1954, in Syracuse (vs. Philadelphia Warriors)
  • March 3, 1955, in Saratoga Springs (vs. Milwaukee Hawks)
  • March 13, 1956, in Moorhead, MN (vs. Minneapolis Lakers)
  • January 17, 1957, in Lacrosse, WI (vs. Minneapolis Lakers)
  • January 14, 1958, in St. Louis (vs. Cincinnati Royals)
  • February 21, 1958, in Camden, NJ (vs. Philadelphia Warriors)
  • January 22, 1962, in Moline, IL (vs. Chicago Packers)
  • March 12, 1962, in Seattle (vs. Los Angeles Lakers)
  • Various times in Hershey, PA (including the Wilt 100 game)

Pistons, 16 games (2020-24)

We’ve seen a new standard of excellence for the Knicks since the turn of the decade, They have three of these streaks in the last six years!

Back when the Pistons weren’t the annoying playoff contenders we know them as now, they were pretty damn awful. For years, it was a running joke that the COVID-19 pandemic was younger than the last Pistons win over the Knicks.

The streak began on February 8, 2020, when the Knicks overcame an early double-digit deficit to outlast the Pistons in Detroit in a battle of two lowly teams that wouldn’t even be invited to the bubble. Another win on March 8 would mark the team’s final home game with fans for another year due to the pandemic.

As the Knicks ascended, the Pistons stayed bad. On April 4, 2021, the Knicks eviscerated them by a 125-81 margin, the second-biggest blowout in the over 430 games in this matchup.

Even as the meltdown in 2021-22 ensued, the orange and blue survived a scare that March when Marvin Bagley III dropped 27, only for Alec Burks to strip Cade Cunningham in the final seconds to hold on.

The most memorable game of the streak came at the end. Facing the 8-48 Pistons at home in late February, the Knicks came out sleepy and watched as Cunningham nearly dragged his hapless team to the finish line to end the skid at 14, but shenanigans ensued with Donte DiVincenzo to somehow pull it off with a Josh Hart and-1.

Was it a foul? Does anyone really care?

The streak ended on December 7, 2024. We didn’t know it at the time, but the Pistons had finally emerged as threats, and they’d start their own six-game regular-season winning streak against the Knicks that lasted until three weeks ago.

Raptors and Nets, 15 games (active)

The last time the Raptors beat the Knicks? January 22, 2023.

The last time the Nets beat the Knicks? January 28, 2023.

The next opportunity for both to beat the Knicks? Brooklyn gets another chance on December 27, while Toronto next gets a crack on January 20. It’ll be basically four years for both since their last win.

These two streaks are tied for the fourth-longest active streaks in the NBA.

The three longer? OKC over Memphis, Cleveland over Washington, and the Clippers over the Hornets, all at 17. If you thought four years was a lot, it’s been almost 10 since the Hornets beat the Clippers!

These two streaks are very different, but also the same. Both teams have been worse than the Knicks this entire time, sometimes considerably worse, and have yielded some ugly blowouts.

There have also been plenty of scares. There’s the Brunson game-winner in the NBA Cup, the KAT heroics in The Six, the times that Brooklyn puts up a fight but folds late at Barclays Center, and the multiple double-digit comebacks we saw this week.

Either way, those are two Atlantic Division rivals that can’t beat the Knicks. It also comes directly after both dominated the Knicks for prolonged periods.

Remember Nic Claxton’s comments? Well, at the time, the Knicks were 0-9 against the Nets from 2020-23.

The Raptors went a blistering 23-5 against the Knicks from January 2016 to November 2023.

Ain’t no fun when the rabbit’s got the gun.

items.title: 24 teams come together to form Collective Cycling Group, the latest venture aiming to 'unlock the value' of pro cycling
items.author: laura.weislo@futurenet.com (Laura Weislo)
items.content:
Following the collapse of the One Cycling project that aimed to reform professional cycling into a more lucrative business model, a new group has officially made its presence known with similar aims but stronger support. The Collective Cycling Group (CCG) issued a press release on Wednesday announcing the new movement.

It was stated that 24 teams from the men’s and women’s WorldTour and ProTeam ranks have already signed up, and that there are ongoing discussions with additional teams. Several teams have shared news of the announcement, indicating that they are part of the movement, but not all have.

The CCG aims to "develop and market selected commercial rights and activities to strengthen the economic model of professional cycling", according to the announcement.

It also wants to "unlock the value potential of professional cycling, elevate the product to better serve a global fan base, and address the need for a more sustainable economic model in professional road cycling and the broadening of its global reach".

The company is registered in the UK and is essentially the same entity as One Cycling, with government files showing the name was changed to Collective Cycling Group on June 2, 2026.

Soon after, ownership of the project changed hands, with Visma-Lease a Bike team boss Richard Plugge standing down both as a 'director' and 'a person with significant control', and replaced in both cases by Oliver Ciesla, a sports marketing executive who previously worked in motorsport.

"This broad and inclusive initiative by so many teams represents a significant milestone in the long and proud history of the sport," Ciesla said.

"Teams carry much of the sporting and financial risk in professional cycling, while many of the sport’s commercial opportunities remain fragmented. The UCI reform process creates a first opportunity to address these challenges together.

"Through a closer cooperation with organisers, the UCI and other stakeholders, teams can create products that none could offer alone, enhancing the experience of fans worldwide, increasing the sport’s visibility, and contributing to a sustainable economic model."

It was not stated in the launch announcement which 24 teams have signed up to form the Collective Cycling Group.

Some teams have since publicly shared the announcement, indicating they are on board. Those teams include EF Education, which has men’s and women’s WorldTour squads, Canyon-SRAM, and Pinarello-Q36.5.

Given Richard Plugge’s prominent role in One Cycling and the push for reform more generally, it can reasonably be assumed that Visma-Lease a Bike are part of the project.

According to , 13 of the 18 men’s WorldTour teams have signed up. The five absentees were said to be UAE Team Emirates-XRG, Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe, Netcompany-Ineos, Jayco-AlUla, and Groupama-FDJ United.

Revamping pro cycling's business model has been a decades-long ambition for many of the stakeholders of a sport

Tour de France owners Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO) are one of the few to be profiting off the sport.

The UCI's formation of the ProTour (now WorldTour) under Hein Verbruggen could be considered to be one of the first attempts at modernizing pro cycling, although the effort was met with extreme resistance from the ASO.

The WorldTour promised to bring more stability to teams, with three-year guaranteed entry into the biggest races, but the sponsorship model of professional cycling remains on shaky ground.

Teams with billionaire backers and generous budgets dominate the sport, while smaller outfits such as TotalEnergies have had to fight for their lives after sponsors pull out.

Even One Cycling wasn't the first try at a new model: In 2011, the Rothschild financial group were backers of what was then called a 'breakaway league' - the World Series Cycling (WSC), with 14 teams on board.

The Velon group came in 2014, with a more modest ambition to add on-board footage and real-time rider stats to their marketing campaigns. How teams really benefited from being a part of Velon is less concrete, and mainly helps with fan engagement and commercialization.

How the CCG will differ from the previous attempts remain to be seen.

How the new CCG project will be received by the UCI should become more clear after the WorldTour seminar, which runs from December 9-10, 2026.

The topics included calendar and participation, the economic model, fan engagement, safety and integrity.

Some of the ideas floated in the document include shortening Grand Tours to 16 days, budget caps, and joint broadcast rights.

items.title: Primož Roglič will continue racing into 2027 as new team for 'final chapter' is finally revealed
items.author: James Moultrie
items.content:
After months of speculation, Primož Roglič will continue his career into 2027, having signed with NSN Cycling Team on a one-year contract.

The 37-year-old looked to be heading for retirement after his time with Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe came to an end – despite being the reigning European time trial champion and having finished second at the Vuelta a España in September – but with NSN, he has found a place for the final chapter of his storied career.

A five-time Grand Tour winner, Roglič will make up part of the Swiss WorldTour team’s general classification ambitions, alongside fellow new signings for 2027, Richard Carapaz and Lennert Van Eetvelt.

"I always like challenges. That's why I'm here, to take these on together and see what the future brings us," said Roglič on the team's website.

"It took me some time to figure out how to make a chapter in my life where I am peaceful, but the answer is actually simple with the team name: Never Say Never. It feels like the perfect connection.

"I still believe I have some work to do – in both racing and with myself. I have the drive and also the attitude not just to race, but also achieve things."

10 years after his first WorldTour season with LottoNL-Jumbo, former ski jumper Roglič will arrive at NSN as the rider with the most victories among active men's pros at 93, only trailing Slovenian compatriot Tadej Pogačar.

Now into his late 30s, he's raced limited calendars in recent seasons, but can still ramp up his performance for the big occasion at Grand Tours, finishing second at the most recent Vuelta, eighth at last year's Tour de France, and winning his fourth Vuelta title as recently as 2024.

Delighted by bringing in the talents of one of the modern era's best GC riders, NSN revealed their new star signing with a social media post of Roglič following NSN on Instagram.

"Welcoming Primož Roglič to NSN Cycling Team is a hugely exciting moment for our organization. From the first moment we spoke, it was evident that Primož still has a lot of passion for the sport and a drive to be the best he can. It was an easy decision to make," said NSN General Manager Kjell Carlström.

"Primož is one of the outstanding riders of his generation. His achievements speak for themselves, and the opportunity to bring someone with his experience, quality and winning mentality into our team is something we are incredibly proud of.

"This signing reflects the ambition we have for the future. We want to compete at the highest level, challenge for major results and continue building a team capable of achieving great things. We are confident that Primož can play an important role in that journey, and we look forward to seeing him race in NSN colours."

items.title: Broken frame no problem for Lukas Malezsewski, who wins UCI Gravel race after being hit by a driver
items.author: Owen Rogers
items.content:
A broken chainstay proved no problem for Belgian gravel racer Lukas Malezsewski, who won the Greek round of the UCI Gravel World Series last weekend.

Riding for Greg van Avermaet’s GVA Gold team, Malezsewski was just 17km into The Gravel of Marathon race when the incident happened: a driver hit him, breaking the chainstay on the drive side of his Basso bike frame.

But rather than give up, the 25-year-old remounted and raced on, eventually winning the Elite Men’s race more than three minutes ahead of second-placed Kasper Enstad.

In its first edition, The Gravel of Marathon is the first UCI round of the UCI Gravel World Series to be staged in Greece, starting and finishing in the ancient city of Marathon. The Elite men raced over a 95km course, which, though relatively short, comprised more than 1,300m of vertical ascent, with 71% of the course off-road.

Malezsewski was hit by the vehicle after the day’s first climb, and not long after emerging from the route’s second gravel sector. "Got hit by a car after 17km and broke my frame. Still made it to the finish line in first place," Malezsewski wrote in an Instagram post.

Rather than treading the well-worn path to gravel from road racing, Malezsewski is an accomplished mountain bike rider, winning the European junior title in 2019 and the Belgian under-23 title in 2022, though he’s not raced at UCI level since 2024.

While he’s raced occasionally at national and UCI .2 level on the road since then, he’s concentrated on gravel.

And to great effect, winning two UCI races last year and repeating the feat this season, when he won Tartu Rattmaraton in Estonia in mid-September, before finishing in the top six of every other race he started before last weekend’s Greek event.

items.title: 'Tour de France Femmes goal for 2029' – There’s a new US team on the scene, and they have big ambitions
items.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
items.content:
The paperwork has been submitted to the UCI and Dr. Andrea Cyr expects to lead the next US-based Continental women's team, Orange Seal presented by Autowurks, in 2027.

The team will be based in Austin, Texas with a "clear ambition" to become a top-25 team in the world with a majority of riders from the United States, and to earn a place in the Tour de France Femmes by 2029.

"We have high aspirations, but the first step is we're going to be a Continental team for 2027. We want to be a ProTeam in 2028, that's where you start to get a lot of the invites like the Classics and bigger UCI stage racing. Then we have a Tour to France Femmes goal of 2029," Cyr told .

"A lot of this is sparked by my own ambition too. There's some development programmes to get people interested in the sport and then there's WorldTour, but there's nothing in between. I'm in a unique position, with resources and networking to actually put things together. A year ago this was not the plan."

The new team merges Cyr's HigherDOSE-Renova criterium-based programme with the former ROXO Continental women's squad, which last competed in 2024 as Boneshaker Project presented by Orange Seal.

"We didn't want this to just be a one-year adventure. We wanted to do something a little bit more sustainable," Cyr said about the next step after HigherDOSE. "So we started conversations with a management group from Texas. All three of these guys have different roles, they've known each other for like 20 years. I think they have found new vigor and motivation through this too."

Leadership at Orange Seal p/b Autowurks includes former WorldTour rider Chann McRae as head sports director, Austin attorney Todd Reed as team manager, and real estate executive Charlie Tames as co-owner. The trio had most recently been involved in supporting French women's ProTeam Mayenne Monbana My Pie. Justin Kirk will split time as a sports director with the women's team and the Texas Roadhouse elite masters team. This quartet of management, along with Cyr, form the ownership group for the team.

"Our goal is to build a top-25 team in the world with a majority of riders from the United States and the resources to compete in the biggest races. Bringing these programs together gives us an established foundation to build on," Tames said in a team statement after a formal launch party in Austin on November 15.

"The 2027 season is the first step toward our top-25 ambition and our goal of reaching the Tour de France Femmes by 2029."

More than half of the roster will come from HigherDOSE, including Cyr and Seitz, with Marjie Bemis, Elizabeth Dixon and Odette Lynch preserving the foundation created in 2026. The ROXO connection brings Femenina a Guatemala stage winner Kira Payer, as well as additional leadership and resources to support the next stage of growth.

Other new riders include Canadian Jenna Nestman, former Fount Cycling rider Alia Shafi, and Nicole Steinmetz, who previously raced for Cynisca and Virginia's Blue Ridge TWENTY24. According to Cyr, two more riders have been offered contracts and the full roster will be confirmed in the coming weeks.

"American racers are struggling, and it's really struggling on the women's side. I personally started shifting my own goals and my own thinking, and I had a really good result at Pro Road Nationals, a top 10 in the road race, fourth in the crit, and then had a really good result at Philly. I got to thinking, maybe I'm more than just a crit racer," Cyr described to her inspiration to form a new team.

"It was really awesome to have Philly back, and I finished that race [top 15 - Ed.], and I was like, 'That was the best day ever! Like that was my favorite ever.'

"We need more of this, like hard racing with strong teams and strong riders from all over the world. This is what I'm craving, and I know I'm not alone in that. I know a lot of other female racers are probably looking for the same thing."

Once Continental status is confirmed, the team plans to firm the 2027 calendar with UCI races in South America and Europe for the spring, and a return block of racing to Europe in July and August. Key US races will include Redlands Bicycle Classic, Tour of the Gila, USPro Road Nationals and Philadelphia Cycling Classic p/b AmeriGas, as well as a selection of criteriums.

"We want a well-rounded race calendar, but also aware of our short and long-term goals. To achieve our long-term goals, we need to get points and really establish quickly as a strong, confident team," Cyr said.

"It's important to stay engaged with the racing we have here in the U.S., which is a lot of criterium racing. It's good for sponsors."

Orange Seal joins as title sponsor, with Autowurks as presenting sponsor. The team is also supported by bike sponsor Winspace with equipment and apparel partners ABUS, Tifosi, MUMU and Schwalbe.

items.title: Netcompany Ineos lose significant sponsor as TotalEnergies confirms it will not continue in 2027
items.author: Patrick Fletcher
items.content:
With TotalEnergies moving its financial resources away from the eponymous French ProTeam – which will become XEFI in 2027 – and over to one of the leading women's teams, there were question marks over the company's relationship with the Ineos team.

And now a spokesperson has confirmed to that the sponsorship will not continue beyond this season.

"At the conclusion of these two seasons of sponsorship, TotalEnergies would like to thank the Netcompany INEOS team for its commitment and professionalism, as well as all of its riders, who kept us inspired and excited through their sporting achivements," read a statement.

The news will raise new questions over the finances of Netcompany Ineos, especially in light of the ongoing reports of financial headaches at Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos empire, and the general move towards dilution of its sporting projects.

The company gave up its sole title sponsor’s slot at the cycling team this year, as the Danish IT firm Netcompany was welcomed as a major new backer on a five-year deal.

However, Netcompany’s arrival was not the end of the story, with Tom Hill, the team’s chief commercial officer, saying soon after: “We’re going back to market looking for a second co-title partner.”

There were widespread reports since its arrival at the team in 2025 that TotalEnergies were exploring options for escalation of its sponsorship, including here on where we reported earlier this year that co-title sponsorship was under discussion.

The French energy giant had been clear that it would end its 10-year title backing of Jean-René Bernaudeau’s French team at the end of this season, but clearly wanted to stay in cycling elsewhere.

However, the idea of furthering of the Ineos partnership has broken down at some point and the energy company has gone down a different road, throwing its weight into women’s cycling and the French team that’s home to the world’s top rider, Demi Vollering.

It was interesting that the FDJ team’s manager, Stephen Delcourt, told Cyclingnews that the deal with TotalEnergies came together “very, very fast”, with contact first initiated around the Tour de France Femmes and tied up in a ground-breaking five year deal only a matter of weeks afterwards.

Today’s statement confirms that all its eggs are now in that basket, which raises interesting questions surrounding value for money in terms of the amounts required for the various sponsorship tiers comparing men’s and women’s cycling.

As for Netcompany Ineos, there are no serious doubts surrounding their future after Netcompany’s long-term commitment earlier this year, but the breakdown in the TotalEnergies relationship raises question marks, over how the team will reach the sort of funding levels that the team themselves have acknowledged are required to return to super-team status.
